authentication-api.anchor: The message to sign is a concatenation of
authentication-api.body: Signing flow is described, but no SDK or helper is shipped anywhere on the site. Integrators must hand-roll the ISO8601 timestamp + path + method + base64(sha256(body)) concatenation and sign it themselves. Stripe, Plaid, and Paystack all ship language SDKs.

authentication-api.anchor: The message to sign is a concatenation of
authentication-api.body: Publish a TypeScript and Python signing helper (~50 lines each) on npm and PyPI. Cheapest meaningful DX win available.

sandbox-testing-api.body: Success and Failure JSON examples both show only the `settlementInfo` object, and the only field that differs is `walletAddress`. Show the full request payload, or at least call out that `walletAddress` is the only difference.

No JSON examples. The integrator is told to "Include `Successful` anywhere in the sender's name" but isn't shown where in the request body that goes. Add example payloads matching the shape used in the Send section.

europe.body: Europe page lists only France (EUR / IBAN). Almost certainly a licensing constraint rather than a tech one (France gives broad SEPA + IBAN coverage and a French entity unlocks EEA PSP passporting). The interesting question isn't *why France first* but *what's gating the rest of the EU launch*, which is probably country-by-country licensing.

api-transaction-limits.body: `Min Limit` / `Max Limit` cells are denominated in the row's `Currency` value, but neither the column header nor the cell calls that out.

Suffix each cell with the currency code (e.g. `1,000,000 BWP` instead of `1,000,000`). Adding a parallel USD column would help cross-row comparison but introduces FX staleness, so it would need a rendered-at timestamp or a live rate lookup.

channels-api.anchor: If the maximum is 0, then it implies that there is no maximum specified by the provider
channels-api.body: Forces every integrator to special-case `0`. Hard-coding the equivalent local-currency value into the field would be wrong though, since the cap is USD and the field is local, so any baked-in value goes stale with FX.

channels-api.anchor: If the maximum is 0, then it implies that there is no maximum specified by the provider
channels-api.body: Return `null` (or omit the field) when no provider max is set, and add a separate `effectiveMaximumUSD: 20000` field. Document the rule directly in the field description on `GET Channels`, not just in this callout.

networks.anchor: Right now, the API doesn't have a list of all banks available in all countries
networks.body: Probably reflects aggregator architecture (NIBSS in Nigeria, etc.) rather than a Yellow Card data gap. The clearing partner accepts any valid bank code, so YC may not have a clean per-bank list to surface.

networks.anchor: Right now, the API doesn't have a list of all banks available in all countries
networks.body: Current Manual Input flow forces customers to free-type their bank name, which is bad UX and a fat-finger risk for irreversible payouts. That said, every payout that succeeds via Manual Input is implicit evidence that a given bank works.

networks.anchor: Right now, the API doesn't have a list of all banks available in all countries
networks.body: **Cheap:** crowdsourced bank discovery, dropdown sourced from the set of banks YC has historically cleared payments to.

networks.anchor: Right now, the API doesn't have a list of all banks available in all countries
networks.body: **Better:** integrate a third-party bank-code dataset per country (ISO 9362, national BIN / sort-code registries).

kyc-metadata.anchor: Due to the extra regulatory requirements in Nigeria
kyc-metadata.body: Same hand-build-then-validate pattern as the per-country Send fields in Making a Send. Would benefit from the same JSON Schema export.

kyc-metadata.anchor: If a Tier 0 transaction is attempted after the limit is reached
kyc-metadata.body: The error message `Full KYC information is required for the transaction` almost certainly also fires when KYC fields are simply missing on a non-Tier-0 request. Two very different problems (collect more KYC vs. user has burned through their $200 lifetime Tier 0 allowance), same error string, indistinguishable from the response.

kyc-metadata.anchor: If a Tier 0 transaction is attempted after the limit is reached
kyc-metadata.body: Introduce a distinct error code, e.g. `Tier0LimitExceeded` (that's exactly what the `code` field is for). Include `tier0LimitUsdRemaining: 0` in the payload so integrators can render meaningful UI.

list-collections-guide-api.body: `additionalIdType` and `additionalIdNumber` only carry meaning for Nigerian recipients (NIN + BVN). Doc doesn't show whether non-Nigerian responses return `null`, omit the fields, or return empty strings. `null` is the worst of the three: it forces integrators to write `if (x != null)` for a field that cannot meaningfully exist outside one country. Omit them entirely instead.

integration-security-guide.anchor: Regular Rotation of API Keys and Secrets
integration-security-guide.body: Self-serve key rotation flow: create new key, mark old key as expiring in N days (rotate without outage).

integration-security-guide.anchor: Regular Rotation of API Keys and Secrets
integration-security-guide.body: Active-keys list with last-used timestamps so dead keys can be safely revoked.

integration-security-guide.anchor: Regular Rotation of API Keys and Secrets
integration-security-guide.body: Scoped keys (read-only, send-only). The Going Live page hints at "specific permissions" but no UI or API for managing them is documented.
